Topics · Meaning and purpose

Does the Quran talk about caring for the earth?

A set balance, a word against ruin, creatures as communities like us, hope of return. The text and its limits.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ٧ أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْمِيزَانِ٨ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا۟ ٱلْمِيزَانَ٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance That you not transgress within the balance. And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance.

Quran · Ar-Rahman 55:7-9

Translation

“‘You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity. You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin. I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֖וֶל בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט בַּמִּדָּ֕ה בַּמִּשְׁקָ֖ל וּבַמְּשׂוּרָֽה׃ מֹ֧אזְנֵי צֶ֣דֶק אַבְנֵי־צֶ֗דֶק אֵ֥יפַת צֶ֛דֶק וְהִ֥ין צֶ֖דֶק יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:35-36

World English Bible

Look at any living system: water, air and soil, each in measure. Upset one and the others shift. These verses describe something close: He raised the sky and set the balance, then asks people not to exceed it, and to keep the weight fair. Most commentators read balance as justice among people, and a wider reading has its ground too: that fairness is built into the world. A person lives inside that balance, and not above it.

A question for you

Where do you see this balance most clearly?

If you sayIn nature.
ThenThen you are reading the balance widely, and that reading has its own question.
If you sayIn fairness between people.
ThenThat is how most commentators read it. The next verses join the two.
If you sayI do not see one. Nature is harsh.
ThenAn honest observation. The text does not call the world gentle. It says there is measure in it, and that people are not to go beyond.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلَـٰحِهَا وَٱدْعُوهُ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا ۚ إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

Jeremiah · 29:7

World English Bible

﴿وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا طَـٰٓئِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ إِلَّآ أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُم ۚ مَّا فَرَّطْنَا فِى ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ مِن شَىْءٍ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you. We have not neglected in the Register[302] a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.

Translator's notes

[302] The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), in which all things are recorded.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:38

Translation

“But ask the animals now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you. Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you. The fish of the sea will declare to you. Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this, in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?

Original · Hebrew

וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל־נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד־לָֽךְ׃ א֤וֹ שִׂ֣יחַ לָאָ֣רֶץ וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לְ֝ךָ֗ דְּגֵ֣י הַיָּֽם׃ מִ֭י לֹא־יָדַ֣ע בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֥י יַד־יְ֝הוָה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּֽאת׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־חָ֑י וְ֝ר֗וּחַ כָּל־בְּשַׂר־אִֽישׁ׃

Job · 12:7-10

World English Bible

One who damages what was set right tears down work they did not build. The first verse says: do not ruin the earth after it was set right. The second says animals and birds are communities like you. If creatures were mere tools, they would not be called communities. That word changes how one looks: others in this world have a life and a people of their own, and are more than a resource.

A question for you

What does the word communities change in how you see things?

If you sayI feel like a neighbour to them.
ThenA neighbour has rights. What might those mean in eating and in building?
If you sayNot much.
ThenThat is fine. Keep the word; it may come back with the next bird you see.
If you sayI am struck that this is in an old text.
ThenIt agrees with what many traditions carry about kindness to living things.

Part 3 of 3

﴿ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِى ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى عَمِلُوا۟ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned so He [i.e., Allāh] may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:41

Translation

Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

Original · Hebrew

צְדָקָ֥ה תְרֽוֹמֵֽם־גּ֑וֹי וְחֶ֖סֶד לְאֻמִּ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃

Proverbs · 14:34

World English Bible

An act's effect does not stay with its doer. The verse says ruin has appeared on land and sea by what people's hands have earned. It speaks of people in general and of no particular victim, so it is not to be read as blaming those struck by a disaster. Its last words matter most: that they may return. The point of seeing the effect is coming back, which means repair is possible.

A question for you

What small repair is nearest to you?

If you sayIn what I consume.
ThenHere 7:31 has a simple word on excess.
If you sayIn the place where I live.
ThenThat is where building up begins: a particular place.
If you sayI doubt that one person matters.
ThenA real question. The next Step asks how reform can miss its own mark.
